charge_gas(evm, GasCosts.OPCODE_TSTORE)

cls24-tstore-charges-state-gas.why: TSTORE acquires a full state-gas cost (97,920, the same as a fresh storage slot), i.e. a fork decides transient storage is state after all. This is the mutation class #24's immunity arm exists to catch: the immunity is load-bearing for 14,167 deployed addresses and nothing else in the corpus asserts it.

    charge_state_gas(evm, StateGas(Uint(1530)))  # MUTATION

cls24-tstore-charges-one-state-byte.why: TSTORE acquires a state cost of one single state byte (COST_PER_STATE_BYTE = 1530), the smallest state charge the schedule can express. Paired with cls24-tstore-charges-state-gas to grade how small a state charge each arm can see: a tight-literal survival arm cannot, an exact-threshold or reservoir-exhaustion arm can.

cls24-transient-revert-not-rolled-back.replace: pass  # MUTATION: a reverted frame's transient writes survive
cls24-transient-revert-not-rolled-back.why: restore_tx_state no longer rolls transient storage back, so a reverted frame's TSTORE survives. A deployed 'set once per transaction' guard (L2: 2,005 runtimes / 5,478 addresses) would then be bricked for the rest of the transaction by one tolerated failure.

cls24-tload-always-zero.replace: return U256(0)  # MUTATION: transient storage has no visibility
cls24-tload-always-zero.why: TLOAD always reads zero, i.e. transient storage has no lifetime at all. The coarse end of the lifetime pair: every transient reentrancy lock (L2: 2,315 runtimes / 4,528 addresses) stops excluding anything, and no gas number moves.

cls25-origin-is-the-current-caller.why: ORIGIN reports the current frame's caller instead of the transaction sender, so tx.origin == msg.sender becomes a tautology. Every 'called directly by a wallet' gate (L2: 8,097 runtimes / 6,126 addresses) then admits any contract.

cls25-caller-is-the-tx-origin.why: CALLER reports the transaction sender instead of the calling frame. The other direction of the same equality: the gate still admits everything, but msg.sender-based authorisation breaks too. Paired with cls25-origin-is-the-current-caller so the equality is mutated from both sides.

cls25-delegatecall-rewrites-the-caller.why: DELEGATECALL stops passing its own caller through and becomes opaque like CALL. This is the only call-like instruction that preserves the caller (system.py:866), and it is why the invariant has to be stated as 'no frame that rewrites the caller' rather than 'no contract frame'. A fork that 'repaired' tx.origin == msg.sender this way would break every deployed proxy.

cls25-delegation-length-24.why: is_valid_delegation stops recognising the 23-byte designator that set_delegation writes, so the delegation never resolves and the delegated code never runs. Stands in for 'the designator format moved' -- the EIP-7702 hazard that classes #22 (callee side) and #25 (caller side) both depend on is keyed to this one magic number.
